new_scholarship.name: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship (stypendium rektora)
legacy_titles: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship for International Students
new_scholarship.description: Jagiellonian University's Rector's Scholarship is a merit-based cash benefit from the university Scholarship Fund for first-cycle (bachelor), second-cycle (master) and long-cycle master's students, awarded on request for outstanding academic performance, scientific, artistic or sports achievements. In the first year of first-cycle or long-cycle master's studies it goes to students admitted in the year of the matura exam who won an international olympiad or were laureates/finalists of a central-level olympiad, or who medalled in at least a Polish Championship competition; in higher years it is capped at 10% of students in a given programme. Foreign students admitted from the 2019/2020 academic year onward may apply regardless of citizenship. The award runs for nine months (October to June), paid monthly into a Polish zloty (PLN) bank account held at a bank in Poland.

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Enrolled in first-cycle, second-cycle or long-cycle master's studies at Jagiellonian University; not available to students who already hold a master's degree (or a bachelor's degree when re-enrolling in first-cycle studies), including degrees obtained abroad; not available to conditionally enrolled students, students who repeated a year without completing the next one, or students resuming after removal from the student list. Foreign students admitted from 2019/2020 onward qualify regardless of citizenship. Total eligibility is 12 semesters, with a maximum of 9 semesters for first-cycle and 7 for second-cycle studies.

Ties are broken by: points for academic/artistic/sports achievements, then ECTS credits obtained, then the grade average over the entire course of studies, then the admission result for first-year second-cycle students.

new_scholarship.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international master's programmes jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries. They normally run one to two academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS) and award either a single joint degree or multiple degrees from the consortium. The master's consortium may offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide; where offered, these cover participation costs and contribute to travel, visa costs and a living allowance. Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, and a new batch of selected masters is added to the list each year.

programme_detail_official.description: Nova SBE's master's scholarships and funding page sets out an institutional and partner-funded portfolio. The Nova SBE Merit Scholarship is open to every applicant regardless of country of origin and reduces the master's tuition fee by 20% or 50%, with interest declared in the master's application form and the merit criteria re-checked at the end of the first year. The Social Mobility Scholarship (20%, 50% or 100%) supports candidates with proven financial need, and the Continuity Scholarship (50% or 100%) widens that threshold for Nova SBE bachelor's graduates. Partner awards from Accenture, Antonio Serrenho, Banco Primus, Deloitte, Andre Sousa Bessa and others cover 100% of tuition but impose programme, GPA, nationality and income conditions, and some require an interview or video. Scholarships are awarded on a rolling basis because the budget can be used up before the end of the master's admission cycle, and none of them funds the application fee, the enrolment instalment, CEMS, the Double Degree, additional semesters, exchange programmes or Executive Master's programmes. Combined Nova SBE funding is normally capped at 70% of tuition.
